title: GenerationJob
description: Core -> AI service (POST /jobs): one generation job (B7 R1). The service keeps jobs only in memory; the core owns open jobs. request_id is the job id. Sending the SAME job again (same id, same content) is harmless and returns the existing job, e.g. after a lost answer. A NEW attempt (after a failed job, or after the service restarted and answers not_found) always gets a NEW request_id, like Resend for decisions. Same id with different content is rejected (bad_request, not retryable).

request_id.description: Deterministic id from the core; also the job id. New attempt = new id.

tick.description: Tick at which the core created the job.

priority.description: Higher runs first; ties in order of arrival. Values come from data in the core (B7 O2).

inhabitant.description: Inhabitant the job is about, if any.

object.description: Object the job is about, if any.

JobPayload.description: One optional field per job kind; exactly the field named like the kind is set (checked by the service and the core). Unset fields are left out by both type systems (pydantic exclude_unset, C# WhenWritingNull), so a new kind is not a breaking change (review GW1 M1).

QuestionPayload.description: An inhabitant does not understand something and asks (W1595). No deadline (B2487): answered at once on strong PCs, at the latest in the computing night.

question.description: what_is = what is this; can_i_eat; is_dangerous; what_can_i_do = what can I do with it; why = why did this happen.

perception.description: What the inhabitant notices about the subject right now (observable properties only, no truth).

label.description: What THIS inhabitant calls the kind of thing it asks about (subject of kind type), by its own knowledge only: the inhabitants' name of an invention it believes anything about (it invented it, built it, tried it, looked at it, was told about it). Absent when it knows nothing of it, and for things the data name (the id is the vocabulary key, i18n key vocab.object.<id>). Never a truth the inhabitant does not know; resolved when the message is built. Optional (absent also from an older core).

InventionLimits.description: Limits from data (B4b; values from Marcel, placeholders until then).

max_rounds.description: Discussion rounds with the rule guard (B4b: 2).

InventionPayload.description: Invent something (D471 stage 2): the inhabitant wants or found something it has no solution for.

want.description: Need or action the inhabitant has no solution for (vocabulary need or action). With trigger 'idea' it is only the least satisfied need for the record: the prompts (inventor v5, guard v4) take the idea as what is wanted and do not say this want (review GW1 #333).

subject.description: Thing that was found, if the trigger is find.

materials.description: Things in reach as the inhabitant sees them.

tech_level.description: Highest tech level the world allows now.

idea.description: Only with trigger 'idea' (B2578, B4b R28 ripe idea, A1585): the inhabitant's own idea that is ripe - its id, the short English text and what it is built on (subjects of its own knowledge). The inventor answers it and the guard checks the answer against it. Absent otherwise.

BuildPlanPayload.description: Turn an approved invention into a building plan of construction-kit parts (D471 stage 4, ADR-0004).

shapes.description: Part shapes of the construction kit (data).

ProcessPayload.description: An unknown try (B2537): no rule fits these inputs yet. Judged once; the result becomes a world rule. A combine trial (B2687 K2, D932): the inhabitant puts things together without choosing a process - 'process' is null, the core lists the processes whose input/tool shape fits in 'candidates', and the judge says which of them happens, if any.

process.description: The process the inhabitant applies; null for a combine trial (then 'candidates' is set).

signature.description: Canonical signature of this try (true properties, set by the core); the service derives the world rule id from its hash.

candidates.description: Only for a combine trial (process null, B2687 K2): the processes whose input/tool shape fits, listed by the core in the schema's specificity order (more inputs, more properties, tool, heat, id). The judge picks one of them or none (ProcessResult unchanged: rule.process must be one of these). The signature's process is then 'combine', so the same trial is the same world rule whichever process happens. Absent otherwise. Up to 16 since D1025 (GW2 #25006): the core sends every process physics allows, at most physics.max_candidates, so our data rules' ranking never decides which ones the judge sees.

MemoryPayload.description: Memory condensation (B4a R5): the current summary and older events become a new summary within max_chars. English, internal (never shown as is). Formative events must stay in it.

events.description: Events to fold in, oldest first; at least one.

max_chars.description: Hard limit for the new summary (text budget, data in the core).

MemoryFact.description: One event to remember. formative = the core marks it as shaping (pain, first encounter, success; data in the core): it must stay in the summary.

times.description: How often it happened: an everyday event that repeats about the same subject is counted on one entry instead of listed again (data in the core); tick is then the last time. Optional: absent = 1.

outcome.description: What came of it, for a remembered action (absent for other events): done, found_out or nothing. An attempt is not a deed: 'drink' about flint with found_out or nothing means it tried and nothing happened.

label.description: What THIS inhabitant calls the subject (about), by its own knowledge only: the own name of another inhabitant once it has learned it, the inhabitants' name of an invention it knows. Absent when it knows none, and for things the data name (the id is the vocabulary key). Never a truth the inhabitant does not know; resolved when the message is built, so a name learned later shows in earlier events.

SoundPayload.description: A sound for a thing that needs one (B2530, D471 D7): made in the computing night by the local sound model from the rule guard's description; if that fails, the core falls back to the base library.

description.description: Short English description of the sound (from the rule guard's SoundDecision), e.g. 'wooden door creaks'.

seconds.description: Length to make (from content/sound/generation.json by kind).

steps.description: Sampling steps of the sound model (data, D440: at least 25).

object_type.description: The (runtime) object type the sound belongs to, if any.

ImagePayload.description: A picture for a thing (B7 R7, A1408): an icon for the UI or a texture, made in the computing night by the local image model in the game's style. If it fails, the thing keeps the colours and materials of the construction kit.

subject.description: Short English description of what to show, e.g. 'a clay water vessel with a handle' (from the invention). No people, no text.

purpose.description: icon = the thing alone on a plain background (UI); texture = a seamless surface of its main material.

style.description: Style id from the image prompt (e.g. warm_comic, B2501/D355).

object_type.description: The (runtime) object type the picture belongs to, if any.

DreamPayload.description: A dream in the computing night (B7 R8, A1409): a short text in the player's language from the events of the day. The AI only tells the dream and picks a tone from the allowed list; what the dream does (mood, ideas) the core sets through data (content/dreams/settings.json). Shown in the chronicle (B8).

events.description: Events of the day, oldest first (same form as for the memory).

memory.description: The inhabitant's memory summary for background (English, internal; may be empty).

mood.description: Strongest mood at the end of the day (vocabulary moods), or null.

tones.description: Tones the dream may have (from content/dreams/settings.json); the answer names one of them.

max_chars.description: Length limit of the dream text (data).

Model3dPayload.description: Image to 3D model (B7 R9, ADR-0004, A1412): only on the comfort tier (TRELLIS.2, 16-24 GB, Linux). Interface and stand-in only; on other tiers the job fails as not retryable and the construction-kit builder is used.

image_file.description: Picture of the thing from an image job (file name in the service's image folder, no path).

object_type.description: The (runtime) object type the model belongs to, if any.

max_triangles.description: Upper bound for the mesh (data, low-poly style).

ReviewIdea.description: An idea the inhabitant already has (B2578, B4b R28): its id in the core, a short English text (internal, never shown as is), its roots (subjects of its own knowledge, or other ideas by id) and how grown it is.

ReviewPayload.description: The nightly look back of one inhabitant (A1584, B7 R18-R22, B2592, B2687): it replaces memory and dream. From the day's events, the memory, what the inhabitant knows (its Fundbuch, B2589) and its ideas, the AI writes the new memory summary, a dream, new or grown ideas, intentions for the morning and the morning mood. What ideas and intentions do the core decides from data; the review never changes the character (R19).

events.description: The day's events, oldest first (as for memory and dream).

memory.description: The current memory summary (English, internal; may be empty).

mood.description: Strongest mood at the end of the day, or null.

knowledge.description: What the inhabitant believes (its Fundbuch, B2589), cut by relevance in the core; only beliefs, never the truth. Roots of ideas and the subjects of intentions must come from here.

ideas.description: The inhabitant's current ideas (may be empty).

needs.description: Needs at the end of the day (0 = urgent, 1 = satisfied).

traits.description: Character traits (creativity: how often and how bold; curiosity: trying out - B2578, no new trait).

actions.description: Actions an intention may name (vocabulary, general ones).

MilestonePayload.description: R35 (B2598, A1583, D962): a milestone was reached - the chronicle gets one calm sentence for it, written once, in the player's language. The milestone's text key names it in both languages (the base line stays the truth); null sentence = none (content guard or grounding, R24/B2644); a late or failed job leaves the milestone without a sentence.

made.description: The thing made, by the maker's name for it, or null (a rule without a thing).

inhabitants.description: Who reached it, the maker first, by the names they have.

day.description: Game day it was reached (1 = the first).

things.description: Other things that took part (a rule's inputs, e.g. spark and dry grass for a fire), by the maker's names for them; the sentence may name these too. Optional; absent = none.

MilestoneName.description: Something the sentence may name, by the name the maker knows it by (its label from its beliefs, never the truth id), with the id it stands for.
